value_text: The separate AIIMS MBBS entrance was last held in 2019. Since 2020, MBBS admission at every AIIMS is through NEET-UG, with seats allotted in MCC counselling.
The JIPMER MBBS entrance was last held in 2019. Since 2020, MBBS admission at JIPMER is through NEET-UG and MCC counselling.
BHU no longer holds its own medical entrance. MBBS/BDS admission at IMS-BHU is through NEET-UG and MCC counselling.
AMU no longer holds a separate MBBS entrance. MBBS/BDS admission at AMU (JNMC) is through NEET-UG; AMU runs its own counselling for its seats.
KVPY was discontinued in 2022 and merged into the DST INSPIRE scheme. Students in basic science courses can apply for the INSPIRE-SHE scholarship instead.
UPSEE (later UPCET) is no longer the route into AKTU colleges. AKTU now admits B.Tech students on JEE Main ranks and other courses through CUET, with counselling by AKTU.
TISSNET is no longer held. Since 2024, TISS admits to its master's programmes through CUET-PG scores, followed by TISS's own assessment.
ICSI replaced the CS Foundation programme with the CS Executive Entrance Test (CSEET) in 2020. Students now enter the CS course by passing CSEET.
LSAC discontinued LSAT India after the 2024 tests; there is no LSAT India in 2025 or 2026. Colleges that used it now accept other tests (for example CLAT, CUET-UG or their own tests).
IRTS has been merged into the Indian Railway Management Service (IRMS). Railway management officers are now recruited through the UPSC Civil Services Examination.
RPET is no longer held. Rajasthan B.Tech admission runs through REAP, which ranks candidates mainly on JEE Main scores (a separate merit list uses Class 12 marks).
NTSE has not been held since the 2021 cycle; NCERT put the scheme on hold and has not announced a new cycle. Watch ncert.nic.in for any restart.
